statement: Amr ibn al-Harith (brother of his wife Juwayriyah): he left no dirham, dinar, slave or anything else except his white mule, his weapons and land he had given as charity.
Aishah: he died with his armour pledged for thirty sa' of barley.
He said: we are not inherited from; what we leave is charity.
notes: Direct speech. Machine-checked (quoted by Abu Bakr).

statement: Aishah, asked about his character: 'Do you not read the Qur'an? The character of the Prophet of Allah was the Qur'an.'
notes: Direct speech. Content machine-checked in the Muslim dataset (no. 1739); Abd al-Baqi number from memory.

statement: Anas: I served him ten years; he never said 'uff' to me, nor 'why did you do that' or 'why did you not do that'.
He said: the best of you is the best to his family, and I am the best of you to my family.
notes: Direct speech. Machine-checked; graded sahih (al-Albani, Ahmad Shakir).

statement: At Ta'if he declined the destruction of those who harmed him and hoped for their descendants.
At the conquest of Makkah he granted its people safety.
After Hunayn he returned the captive families of Hawazin.
At Arafah he said he had left among them the Book of Allah.
The Qur'an was written by his scribes and memorised in his lifetime, and gathered into one collection under Abu Bakr.
He said: convey from me, even if it is one verse.
